## Engineering problem

Drainage and flood information for Bangkok is published by several agencies in different formats, with different update rates and often without a clear distinction between when a value was measured and when it was retrieved. That makes it hard to judge whether a displayed value is current or reliable.

## System requirements

- Aggregate heterogeneous public sources while preserving source provenance and byte-exact raw snapshots.
- Keep **measurement time** separate from **retrieval time**, and never back-fill unknown timestamps.
- Classify source health and data freshness, including stale, failed, unknown and static-only records.
- Never invent coordinates, units, datums or timestamps.

## System architecture

```
config/sources.yaml ─► adapter.healthcheck() ─► adapter.fetch() ─► raw snapshot (immutable)
                                                                         │
                                               adapter.normalize() ◄─────┘
                                                        │  schema validation
                                                        ▼
                                   de-duplication on (source, station, variable, measurement time, value)
                                                        ▼
                                         SQLite database ─► Streamlit interface (read-only)
```

## Implementation and design decisions

- Registry of 795 stations, 582 of them with coordinates, served through five source adapters.
- Time-to-live caching and merging of database, static and live data.
- Source-health and data-freshness classification with geographic and status filters.
- Raw payloads are written before parsing and never overwritten; every transformation (declared time zone, declared units, ambiguous dates) is flagged rather than silently applied.

## Tools and technologies

Python, SQLite, Pydantic validation, Streamlit (deployed on Streamlit Community Cloud).

## Validation and limitations

Adapters that cannot retrieve data reliably report their state as manual or unavailable and insert nothing. No hydraulic or drainability metric is computed before model validation. See the repository documentation for the current status of each source.

## Documentation

Architecture, data model and source policy are documented in the [repository](https://github.com/poundthammaratx/bangkok-drainability-observatory).
